title: Every build passes through the safety pipeline
content: BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL -> QA -> FINAL REGRESSION AUDIT -> CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING -> HUMAN LAUNCH APPROVAL -> LIVE. No stage may be skipped by an agent.

title: GREEN / AMBER / RED permission tiers
content: GREEN actions run automatically. AMBER actions require explicit human approval before execution. RED actions (DNS, registrar, payment credentials, destructive infrastructure) are never executed by an agent without explicit, named authorization.

title: Launch never auto-approves
content: QA at zero is necessary, never sufficient, for launch. Launch requires human approval; approving with open launch holds is a deliberate, recorded human decision.

title: Agents propose; humans approve knowledge
content: Agents may propose lesson candidates. No agent may promote its own output into AGENCY or DOCTRINE knowledge. Human approval is the only path from CANDIDATE to APPROVED.

title: U-Proof prior Creative Touch audit history (as of 2026-09-02)
content: Creative Touch's own prior hands-on technical audit history for this project (most recent pass 2026-09-02): no shipping zones/methods configured (test order confirmed silent no-shipping checkout, since deleted); only BACS/Cheque/COD enabled, Paystack/Payflex installed but never configured with real credentials; compiled Shop/Product/Cart/Checkout build files were found hardcoding a third-party 10Web trial domain (allowed-pony.10web.cloud) for logo/breadcrumb/footer/payment-icon assets, confirmed live and customer-facing as of 2026-09-02, then stripped from on-disk build files in a housekeeping pass (not independently re-verified live since); a fake 'recent articles' teaser section (FAQs, How to Apply Liquid Rubber, Surface Preparation Guide) on the homepage links to non-existent pages, left from an earlier AI-generated clone; real broken homepage CTA links were found and fixed; a placeholder-style phone number pattern (+27100000000) was noted; WooCommerce shipping-origin address was corrected to match the Contact page's address at the time (Unit 4, Gateway Industrial Park, Sebenza, Edenvale, Johannesburg); order-notification emails were going to Creative Touch's own address rather than the client's business inbox, and the outgoing from-address was a leftover third-party domain - both flagged, not resolved; security hardening was applied (headers, stripped version-disclosure tags, removed exposed backup files); real Size and Size x Color variation structures were built and verified for Liquid Rubber, Fibre Filler, Wall & Roof Paint and Membrane with real pricing. None of this should be assumed still accurate without checking fresh evidence - several items already appear to have changed.

title: U-Proof business context
content: The client (Martin) owns a South African waterproofing/building-products company, U-Proof. Creative Touch is rebuilding/completing the company's ecommerce website on WordPress + WooCommerce after a prior developer relationship broke down without a proper handover. The client likes the existing design and wants it completed and improved, not redesigned. The client does not want manual/flat-rate shipping and prefers live courier rates (Fastway Couriers); Payflex (SA buy-now-pay-later) was under evaluation alongside a standard card gateway, because the client does not want EFT/manual payment as the primary path.
